name: NY-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: District fundamentals are overwhelmingly Democratic, with a D+33 partisan lean
Micah Lasher holds a massive financial edge, with $3.4 million raised and over $10 million in outside support
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 98% to win
Open seat after Jerry Nadler's retirement, but the seat remains safely in Democratic hands
model.rationale: The district's D+33 fundamentals make a Republican win implausible, and nothing in the evidence points the other way: Lasher has outraised Shinkle by roughly fourteen to one and enjoys heavy outside backing, while markets price the Democratic side near 98%. The forecast stays anchored to the strong fundamentals with a modestly wider margin than the combined baseline given the open seat.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or an unexpected scandal involving Lasher would be the main things that could narrow this margin, though even a large shift would likely leave the seat Democratic.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New York's 12th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, and Jerry Nadler's retirement does not change that underlying reality. Micah Lasher enters the general election as the heavy favorite, backed by a fundraising operation that has dwarfed Republican Caroline Shinkle's effort and by more than ten million dollars in outside support on the Democratic side.

Shinkle has raised about a quarter of a million dollars, a figure unlikely to move the needle in a district this blue. Independent candidates on the ballot trail far behind in both money and visibility. Prediction markets reflect the lopsided nature of the race, pricing the Democratic nominee near 98%. With no public polling and no expert ratings to complicate the picture, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold in this open-seat contest.
